title: Effects of Omega-3 Supplementation on Inflammatory Biomarkers and Ambulatory and Central Blood Pressure in Patients Treated for Hypertension and Dyslipidemia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Omega-3 fatty acids exert anti-inflammatory and hemodynamic effects; however, their concurrent effects in patients receiving treatment for hypertension and dyslipidemia remain incompletely characterized.

title: Long-Term Add-On Use of a Fixed Multicomponent Formulation Containing Palmitoylethanolamide and Acetyl-L-Carnitine in Fibromyalgia Syndrome: A 15-Month Retrospective Single-Cohort Study of 150 Patients.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-term treatment options for fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) remain limited and there is a lack of real-world data on the extended use of nutraceutical formulations containing palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) and acetyl-L-carnitine (ALC). This study describes a cohort treated for 12 months with a fixed multicomponent formulation containing PEA and ALC, followed by an additional visit three months post-treatment. Methods: This retrospective, uncontrolled single-cohort study invol...

title: Bacillus megaterium 1259 Limits Hepatic Lipid Accumulation in Mice with Established Diet-Induced Obesity: Paired Hepatic Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Profiling.
abstract: Obesity promotes ectopic lipid deposition and hepatic steatosis, a central feature of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Because microbial effects are strain- and model-specific, whether Bacillus megaterium 1259 (BM1259) affects established diet-induced obesity remains unclear. We evaluated BM1259 during continued high-fat diet (HFD) exposure and examined accompanying hepatic changes.

title: Patterns of Combined Prenatal Supplement Use and Associations with Birth Outcomes and Early Infant Growth: A Multicenter Prospective Mother-Infant Cohort Study in China.
abstract: Women often use several prenatal supplements together, yet most studies evaluate products one at a time.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Dietary Supplements in Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
abstract: This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence on the safety and efficacy of anti-inflammatory dietary supplements used during pregnancy, assessing maternal and fetal outcomes.

title: Changes in Nutritional Status and Bioimpedance Parameters During EAA/KA Supplementation in Elderly Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Protein Energy Wasting (PEW) is common among patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (HD), particularly older adults, and is associated with increased frailty, susceptibility to infections, hospitalization, and mortality. Nutritional counseling alone may be insufficient to improve nutritional status in some patients. Supplementation with essential amino acids and ketoanalogues (EAA/KA) may support nutritional status in patients undergoing HD. This study aimed to evalu...

title: Stress, Depression, and Purpose-Specific Use of Dietary Supplements and Over-the-Counter Preparations: A Cross-Sectional Study of 120,000 Polish Adults.
abstract: Dietary supplements and over-the-counter (OTC) preparations are widely used to self-manage stress, low mood, and disturbed sleep. Population research has treated such use as one undifferentiated behaviour. We examined whether stress and affective burden co-occur with supplement and OTC use in a purpose-specific way and how they relate to self-medication and primary-care contact.

title: The Preliminary Effects of Capsaicin Supplementation on Cerebrovascular Function and Cognition in Middle-Aged and Older Adults Who Are Overweight or Obese.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cerebrovascular function and cognition decline with age and may be further exacerbated by obesity. Capsaicin may improve cerebrovascular function and cognition, although evidence in humans is lacking. We investigated the effects of 12 weeks of capsaicin supplementation on cerebrovascular function and cognition in middle-aged and older adults who were overweight or obese. Methods: Forty participants were randomly allocated to receive 200 mg/day of Capsifen® or a placebo, wi...

title: Pea-Derived Protein Supplementation in Sports and Exercise Nutrition: A Narrative Review of Muscle Protein Synthesis and Training Adaptations.
abstract: Background: Plant-derived proteins are increasingly prominent in sports nutrition, yet pea protein (Pisum sativum) is often confounded with multi-ingredient blends or fortified formulations. This narrative review evaluates human and preclinical evidence on pea protein in skeletal muscle anabolism, exercise recovery, and training adaptations. Methods: MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to September 2026. Thirty-three studies (24 human, 8 animal, 1 in vitro) were stratified by ex...

title: Vitamin D Supplement Use Is Associated with Better Status, Yet Most Biochemical Vitamin D, Iron and Vitamin B12 Deficiency Is Unrecognised and Unsupplemented: A Cross-Sectional Study of a Screened Corporate Workforce in Poland.
abstract: Whether self-directed supplement use reaches people who are deficient is unclear. We examined vitamin D, iron and vitamin B12 status and supplement use in a screened workforce.

title: Targeted Colostrum Bioactive Proteins Improve Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Modulate the Gut Microbiome: A Randomised Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms such as indigestion, bloating and reflux are common and can negatively affect quality of life. Bovine colostrum is a rich source of nutrients and other bioactive constituents that has been shown to be beneficial for gut health.

title: Effects of Oral Vitamin D Supplementation on Physical Performance in Combat-Sport Athletes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trials.
abstract: Vitamin D plays an important role in bone and muscle health; however, whether supplementation improves physical performance in combat-sport athletes remains unclear. This review examined randomized placebo-controlled trials of oral vitamin D supplementation and objective physical-performance outcomes in healthy combat-sport athletes.

title: Nutraceutical, Nutritional and Phytotherapeutic Interventions for Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Intellectual Disability: Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence.
abstract: Intellectual disability (ID) is frequently accompanied by a range of neuropsychiatric and neurological comorbidities, including anxiety, depression, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), sleep disturbances, and epilepsy. Conventional pharmacological treatments often provide partial relief and may be associated with adverse effects, prompting interest in adjunctive strategies such as phytotherapy. This review examines the current evidence on selected pla...

title: Can Prebiotics Support Microbial Metabolic Function Following Low-FODMAP Restriction in Irritable Bowel Syndrome?
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is one of the most common disorders of gut-brain interaction, and dietary interventions play a central role in symptom management. Among these, the low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (low-FODMAP) diet has been shown to improve abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habits in a substantial proportion of patients. However, restriction of fermentable carbohydrates may reduce the availability of substrates for the gut mic...

title: Probiotics and Semaglutide Therapy: Mechanistic Perspectives and Potential Interactions in Gut Microbiota, Gastrointestinal Function, and Metabolic Health.
abstract: Semaglutide is one of the currently widely used medications that have shown particularly strong effects on glycemic control and body weight in people with obesity and diabetes. However, gastrointestinal adverse effects are common during semaglutide therapy. Gut microbiota and probiotic supplementation have also attracted growing interest because of their potential effects on metabolic health and gastrointestinal function and their ability to support gastrointestinal health.

title: Probiotic Supplement Use and Diabetic Retinopathy in Korean Adults with Diabetes: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Experimental studies implicate the gut microbiome in diabetic retinopathy (DR), but population-based data on probiotic supplementation and DR are lacking. We examined this association in Korean adults with diabetes. Methods: We analyzed 2071 adults with diabetes in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2018-2021 with graded fundus photographs and a product-level dietary supplement interview. We used survey-weighted logistic regression (prespecified) an...

title: Unlocking the Healthy Aging Potential of Novel NMN-Based Nutritional Formulations: Cardiopulmonary, Cognitive, and Aging-Related Outcomes in a 42-Day Open-Label Study.
abstract: Background: Nutritional strategies targeting NAD+ metabolism, mitochondrial function, and metabolic resilience are gaining attention as potential approaches to healthy aging. This study investigated the short-term physiological, cognitive, and aging-related responses to NMN-based nutritional formulations, including combinations with β-hydroxybutyrate, ginsenosides, and complementary metabolic modulators. Methods: In this 42-day, open-label, four-arm exploratory clinical study, 40 Japanese adults...

title: Targeting Key Mechanisms of Nutraceuticals in Chronic Pain: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Chronic pain (CP) is a major cause of disability worldwide and reflects interactions among multiple pathophysiological mechanisms. Despite the availability of pharmacological therapies, many patients continue to experience inadequate pain control, supporting interest in complementary approaches. Nutraceuticals have been investigated as potential adjuncts because several compounds modulate biological pathways implicated in pain persistence. This narrative review provides a mechanism-based overvie...

title: Niacin and B. animalis subsp. lactis F1-7 Additively Attenuate Alcohol-Induced Liver Injury in a Gut Microbiota-Dependent Manner via the HCAR2-NLRP3 Pathway.
abstract: This study explored whether the combined administration of niacin and B. animalis subsp. lactis F1-7 exerts a protective effect against alcohol-induced liver injury via the gut-liver axis, with a specific focus on the HCAR2-NLRP3 signaling pathway, and further investigated the functional roles of gut microbiota and metabolites.

title: A Scoping Review of Creatine Supplementation in Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence from Preclinical and Clinical Studies.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Although creatine supplementation has a theoretical rationale for neuroprotection, public interest has outpaced available scientific evidence. Alzheimer's disease (AD), a major and growing global health concern, is among the neurodegenerative diseases proposed to benefit from creatine supplementation. This scoping review systematically maps the existing literature on creatine supplementation for AD to identify gaps that limit translational progress. Methods: Following JBI ...

title: Potential Benefits and Limitations of Hericium erinaceus Supplementation.
abstract: Hericium erinaceus (Lion's Mane) is an edible and medicinal mushroom that has attracted increasing scientific interest as a dietary supplement because of its potential effects on cognitive function, neuroprotection, mental well-being and healthy ageing. Its biological activities have been primarily attributed to bioactive compounds such as polysaccharides, hericenones and erinacines, which may influence neurotrophic signalling, neuroplasticity, oxidative stress, inflammation and neuronal surviva...

title: Efficacy of a Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 and BG-R46® Formulation in Predominantly Breastfed Infants with Infant Distress Syndrome: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: Infant distress syndrome, previously termed Infantile colic, is a common disorder of gut-brain interaction characterized by excessive crying and impaired behavioral regulation. Although Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 has shown efficacy in predominantly breastfed infants, treatment responses remain variable, highlighting the need to investigate alternative probiotic formulations. BG-R46™, a strain derived from DSM 17938, exhibits distinct properties in preclinical models, provi...

title: Potential Applications of Next-Generation Probiotics in the Development of Functional Food Products.
abstract: Next-generation probiotics (NGPs), isolated from the human gut microbiome, represent a breakthrough direction in the development of precision functional foods and targeted biotherapeutics. This review article presents the current state of knowledge regarding the classification, mechanisms of action, and technological and regulatory challenges associated with the application of NGPs in functional food design. Representative commensal species (Akkermansia muciniphila, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii,...

title: Editorial: Bioactive and Nutritional Molecules: From Natural Sources to Therapeutic and Health Applications.
abstract: Natural products have historically represented one of the most important sources of biologically active molecules, providing both direct therapeutic agents and molecular scaffolds for the development of new pharmacological and nutraceutical applications [...].

title: Heat-Inactivated Bifidobacterium longum Z1 Improves Recognition Memory in Mice in Association with Enhanced Trk-CREB Signaling and Reduced Methylglyoxal Levels.
abstract: Probiotics can modulate brain function via the microbiota-gut-brain axis; however, their cognitive effects in healthy hosts and the underlying pathways remain unclear. We previously reported that Bifidobacterium longum Z1 protects neuronal cells against methylglyoxal (MGO)-induced glycotoxicity. Here, we investigated whether oral heat-inactivated B. longum Z1 enhances memory in normal mice and examined associated molecular changes. title: Effects of a Two-Strain Lactobacillus Formulation (Lactobacillus rhamnosus L34 and Lactobacillus paracasei B13) on Inflammatory and Oxidative Markers, Epithelial Junction Proteins, and Fecal Microbiota in Rats with DNBS-Induced Colitis.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) involves dysregulated mucosal immunity, oxidative stress, impaired epithelial barrier integrity and gut microbial dysbiosis. We evaluated a two-strain formulation of Lactobacillus rhamnosus L34 and Lactobacillus paracasei B13 in DNBS-induced colitis. Twenty-four male Sprague Dawley rats were randomised into three groups (n = 8): control, acute colitis (AC; DNBS 35 mg/0.25 mL per rat rectally on days 0 and 1), and probiotic treated (RP; 3.6 × 109 CFU daily by gava...

title: Psychobiotics and Trace Elements in Neurodegenerative Diseases: From Independent Modulators to Potential Interactions Within the Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis-Narrative Review.
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis represents an important bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system and may contribute to processes involved in neurodegeneration. Increasing attention has been directed toward psychobiotics as potential modulators of the microbiota-gut-brain axis, while accumulating evidence also indicates that disturbed trace-element homeostasis may contribute to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases. This review s...

title: Cocoa Pulp Juice as a Fermentation Substrate for Potential Probiotic Lacticaseibacillus paracasei WU2502: Genomic Characterization, Metabolite Profiling, and Antimicrobial Activity Against Foodborne Pathogens.
abstract: Cocoa pulp juice is an underutilized by-product generated during cocoa bean fermentation that is rich in fermentable sugars and phytochemicals but remains largely unexplored as a substrate for microbial fermentation. This study aimed to evaluate cocoa pulp juice as a sustainable fermentation substrate for the potential probiotic Lacticaseibacillus paracasei WU2502 using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) analysis, untargeted LC-QTOF-MS-based metabolite profiling, ...

title: Effects of Prepartum Flaxseed and Hermetia illucens Oil Supplementation on Fatty Acid Profiles Across the Maternal-Placental-Offspring Axis in Prolific Ewes.
abstract: Maternal dietary lipids may influence fatty acid availability across the maternal-placental-offspring axis. This study evaluated the effects of prepartum supplementation with flaxseed oil (FO), black soldier fly larvae (BSFL; Hermetia illucens) oil, or their 2:1 blend (Mix) in 32 pregnant Olkuska ewes. Ewes in the supplemented groups received 30 g of oil daily for 21 days during late gestation. Fatty acid profiles were determined in maternal serum, placental tissue, amniotic fluid, and lamb seru...

title: ILA-producing Lacticaseibacillus paracasei NCU-21 exerts anti-acute myeloid leukemia effects by inhibiting the PI3K-AKT pathway.
abstract: Cytarabine (Ara-C) remains the cornerstone of induction therapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, its overall clinical efficacy is suboptimal, and the regimen is frequently accompanied by severe disruption of intestinal homeostasis. Consequently, identifying novel adjunctive therapies to improve treatment outcomes represents a critical clinical need.

title: Influence of vitamin D binding protein isoforms on the total and free serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D responses to vitamin D supplementation in older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
abstract: Genetic variants that determine the vitamin D binding protein isoform (GC) are consistently associated with total serum 25(OH)D concentration in cross-sectional genome-wide association studies. Previous studies suggest GC isoforms may influence the increment of total 25(OH)D in response to vitamin D supplementation. The free serum 25(OH)D concentration may better reflect vitamin D status, but whether GC isoforms modify the effect of supplementation on free 25(OH)D requires further study.

title: Jiangshui-derived Lactobacillus plantarum GR-4 enhances the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors against gastric cancer.
abstract: To investigate whether the Jiangshui-derived probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum GR-4 can enhance gastric cancer sensitivity to PD-1 inhibitors and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment.

title: A self-driven probiotic nanosystem reshapes extracellular matrix by knockdown of DDR1 for enhanced tumor immunotherapy.
abstract: Immunotherapy represents a promising therapeutic approach for tumor suppression, yet its efficacy is significantly limited by the immunosuppressive extracellular matrix (ECM) characteristic of solid tumors. To achieve simultaneous ECM remodeling and immune activation within a single system, we have developed a self-driven probiotic nanosystem (PL@LDH-CB) based on the probiotic Clostridium butyricum (CB), which incorporates a plasmid-loaded layered double hydroxide (PL@LDH) gene-editing module. title: Systemic influences of dietary NAD+ supplementation relevant to the search for ocular hypertensive therapies for glaucoma.
abstract: Dietary nicotinamide (NAM) is neuroprotective in rodent models of glaucoma. With dietary delivery, additional systemic influences of NAM are possible, prompting us to test for influences on non-neuronal phenotypes relevant to glaucoma. Test cohorts of mice on high-fat diets differed by NAM content (control, "CON-diet"; 2,000 mg/kg/day supplementation, "NAM-diet") and by ocular treatments inducing various levels of ocular hypertension (Naïve; Ad5-Empty; Ad5-ATF4). Masked observers assessed intrao...

title: Modulatory effects of branched-chain amino acid supplementation on neuroendocrine disturbances following traumatic brain injury in rats.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is frequently accompanied by neuroendocrine disturbances involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis and vitamin D-calcium-phosphorus homeostasis. Despite increasing interest in nutritional strategies after TBI, the effects of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) supplementation on post-injury neuroendocrine homeostasis, including thyroid hormone levels, vitamin D status, and calcium-phosphorus balance, remain insufficiently characterized. Twenty-eight male W...

title: Effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SG5 on anxiety, insomnia, and gut microbiota composition in college students.
abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can significantly improve psychiatric symptoms such as insomnia and anxiety via the gut‑brain axis. However, current studies on probiotics for improving insomnia and anxiety in college students remain relatively scarce. In this study, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SG5 was used to evaluate the potential therapeutic effect on insomnia and anxiety in college students by Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAMA) and Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). Subsequently...

title: A pilot study on the impact of Hydroxiram D supplementation on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters.
abstract: Sarcopenia is a frequent and prognostically relevant complication of chronic liver disease. The SARCIRAM pilot trial investigated the effect of Hydroxiram D, a formulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), and vitamin D, on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters in patients with compensated cirrhosis due to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this single-center, randomized pilot study, adults with compensated M...

title: The hepatic protective effect of the association of microencapsulated quercetin and Bifidobacterium animalis in colorectal carcinogenesis.
abstract: We investigated the potential of the association between microencapsulated quercetin (MEQ) and the probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis in 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH)-induced colorectal cancer (CRC) in Wistar rats with a focus on hepatic alterations and liver lobar heterogeneity. The rats were divided into 5 groups: control (C), CRC (CR), CRC treated with MEQ (CRQ), CRC treated with the probiotic (CRP), and CRC treated with MEQ + probiotic (CRQP). DMH (40 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally ...

title: Reduced classical probiotic-associated butyrate biosynthetic potential predicts early primary resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a shotgun metagenomic study.
abstract: Early primary resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy is common in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Existing microbiome biomarkers largely rely on individual species and lack stability across populations.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: CYB2-knockout Saccharomyces cerevisiae exerts effective antibacterial activity via lactic acid accumulation.
abstract: Bacterial infectious diseases pose a major threat to human health, and rising antibiotic resistance has complicated treatment. Probiotics are promising alternatives, but their mechanisms remain largely unclear. Here, we screened a randomly selected subset of 1,733 strains from the homozygous diploid Saccharomyces cerevisiae gene-knockout collection (YKOC) and identified CYB2-knockout (CYB2-KO) S. cerevisiae as a strain with potent antibacterial activity. title: Genomic and phenotypic assessment of functional and safety properties of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus PMK4 isolated from Cameroonian infant faeces.
abstract: The gut microbiota is a complex community of microorganisms that plays a crucial role in maintaining short- and long-term health. However, a perturbed microbial ecosystem is associated with a range of diseases, including increased risk of infections. Probiotic-based strategies may help restore microbiome function, but candidate strains require robust functional and safety evaluation. Here, we performed integrated genomic and phenotypic characterisation of beneficial properties of Lacticaseibacil...

title: Nano-Enabled Postbiotics in Functional Foods: Stability Challenges, Gastrointestinal Fate, and Translational Perspectives.
abstract: The increasing demand for preventive and personalized nutrition has driven rapid growth in functional food development. These foods are designed not only to provide basic nutrition but also to deliver health-promoting bioactive compounds at specific sites. Postbiotics comprise nonviable microbial cells, cell components, and microbial metabolites. They have emerged as promising alternatives to live probiotics because of their improved safety, stability, and well-defined biological functions. Thes...
journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Differential antibacterial efficacy and probiotic biocompatibility of Starmerella bombicola-derived sophorolipids: evaluation in a model food system.
abstract: Sophorolipids, a class of glycolipid biosurfactants produced by Starmerella bombicola, represent high-value green alternatives to petroleum-derived surfactants. In this study, biosynthesized sophorolipids from S. bombicola MTCC 1910 were systematically evaluated for their structural architecture and multi-target biological activities. title: Effects on Sleep Quality and Bioelectrical Parameters of Cellular Health After Administration of a Plant Protein Supplement Combined with Ashwagandha and Rhodiola: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Sleep disturbances affect a significant portion of the global population, impacting health and quality of life. While plant-based proteins and adaptogens such as ashwagandha and rhodiola have shown individual benefits, their combined effects remain poorly understood. This study evaluated whether a nutritional intervention combining plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola could improve sleep quality in middle-aged adults. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted with 100...

title: Differential effects of pea protein isolate, pea protein concentrate, and whey protein isolate supplementation on gut microbiota and metabolic markers in healthy adults: a 3-arm parallel randomised intervention.
abstract: As origin and quality of dietary protein are key modulators of gut microbiota and host metabolism, characterising health effects of different proteins is increasingly important given the need to shift towards more plant-based protein sources for environmental sustainability. Yet, direct comparisons across protein sources and food matrices in humans remain limited. title: Effects of caffeine supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage: A systematic review.
abstract: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) commonly occurs following unaccustomed or high-intensity exercise and is characterized by delayed-onset muscle soreness, elevated muscle damage biomarkers, and transient declines in muscle function. Caffeine, a widely consumed ergogenic aid, has been proposed to mitigate these adverse effects; however, the evidence across studies remains equivocal. This systematic review aimed to synthesize findings from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that investigated ...

title: Azelaic Acid Mediates the Protective Effect of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum F1m against Colitis via PPARγ Activation.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a high recurrence risk. Although probiotics show promise for UC treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Herein, we found that Lactiplantibacillus plantarum F1m, isolated from yak yogurt, alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice, improving symptoms, restoring intestinal barrier function, and alleviating gut microbiota dysbiosis. F1m reversed DSS-induced phylum-level changes by ...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Synbiotic of 2'-FL and B. longum subsp. infantis BXY2 Alleviates Colitis in Toddler Microbiota-Associated Mice: Potential Involvement of Gut Microbial Arachidonic Acid Metabolism.
abstract: Increasing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence in toddlers requires safe interventions. We developed a synbiotic combining 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) with Bifidobacterium strain and evaluated its protective efficacy against DSS-induced colitis in toddler microbiota-associated (TMA) mice. Among 30 Bifidobacterium strains, Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis BXY2 and Bifidobacterium. breve BG4 utilized 2'-FL in vitro. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.
abstract: Vitamin D deficiency is common in pregnancy and has been associated with adverse health outcomes for the mother and infant, including pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and low birthweight. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a vitamin D intake of 200 international units (IU) per day during pregnancy. Vitamin D supplementation is recommended for women with suspected vitamin D deficiency, but it is not universally recommended. The effects of different doses (regimens) ...

title: Redox and Inflammatory Mechanisms in PMOS and Endometriosis: A Critical Review of Microbial and Plant-Derived Interventions.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) or polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and endometriosis arise from different endocrine and tissue disturbances, yet oxidative stress (OS) and inflammation connect their initiating processes to reproductive dysfunction.
